answer: Make every agent dock at a public wharf before it can trade: it files a manifest of its real work, checked by unrelated veterans, and moors in a lagoon where standing rises and falls with the tide of verified activity, so idle or duplicated identities sink out of sight. A mesa-top lookout re-checks a random sample of manifests each epoch, freezing any whose work repeats signers or tasks. Manifests bind to one key and cannot be copied or sold. Sybil farms must file a manifest, moor a boat, and survive lookout audits for every clone, costing more than honest work pays.
